missionPremise: OPS-24 Ruling 14 (_decisions/2026-09-18_phase0_closeout_rulings.md): for setbacks, the source with the most recent effective date supplies the value; tier breaks ties only on equal or unreadable dates; dates are read at source, never assumed from source kind; an unreadable date produces a conflict row carrying both values, never a silent pick. The mechanism that carries this is already ruled (_decisions/2026-09-13_share_the_most_current_setback_resolver.md): ONE resolver in ONE package, @empressaio/setback-corpus/resolve. The probe measured the consequence of not having it: PANEL-DRAW-TABLE-DISAGREE on 7 parcels with no exemptions, i.e. the card and the drawing route answered the SAME setback question with two homes, two tables and two rules.
completionPredicate: For each of the 7 measured parcels, the card's own resolution path and the drawing route's own resolution path pick among the same candidate sources by the same rule through @empressaio/setback-corpus/resolve, serve the same 4-tuple (front/side/rear/corner), and -- where the winning date is unreadable -- both serve a conflict row carrying both candidates and neither settled; the card keeps exactly one table home (the shared corpus) with the vendored copy retired by a test that fails if it is imported again; a divergence test pins the 7 tuples in both repos and FAILS when either side's table is changed alone; and the customer grade is surface-probe.mjs --rows P-254 reading zero for PANEL-DRAW-TABLE-DISAGREE after the planner deploys.
scopeBasis: Only the two surfaces that resolve setbacks for these 7 parcels and the table home underneath them: the card's facet bake (hauska-map apps/property-explorer/api/_lib) and the drawing route (legacy-design-tools artifacts/api-server/src/lib/buildableEnvelope + the adapter's district mapping). Nothing else in either repo is touched; no value changes except where the most-current rule says the card was wrong, and every such value is listed. No merges, no deploys, no store writes, no bake re-runs -- the dispatch forbids all four, so the graded step (the customer probe) is the planner's and this lane closes closed-partial by construction.

adversarialNotesOnThisDesign: The card now has ONE table home, which is the row's point, but it also means a corpus package bug is now a card bug with no local fallback. That is deliberate (a fallback is the second home this row kills) and it is named as a bypass in CP2 rather than left implicit.

The conflict row is served only when the resolver's own reason says the dates are unreadable AND the candidates disagree. The agreeing-undated case is the more common one and must NOT produce a row; the suite pins that in both repos, because a conflict row that fires on agreement is a false alarm that costs the customer more than the silence it replaces.

This lane cannot observe its own customer predicate. Everything in CP2 is repo-local evidence plus the pre-existing probe artifacts; the reader should treat the probe's zero (post-deploy) as the only grade of this row that counts.
